gates.label: DB script self-tests
gates._note: Two `--self-test` flags, one gate row: scripts/backup-db.sh and scripts/restore-db.sh each gained one in the same commit, and they are the same defect. A sqlite3 .backup DESTINATION embedded in a dot-command is NOT path-translated by MSYS2 (measured on MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200 with sqlite3 3.50.6), so an absolute path failed with a bare `cannot open /c/...` and the restore ABORTED at its own pre-restore safety step -- the worst possible place for a path bug. Both scripts' documented invocations are RELATIVE (backup-db.sh header :9-12), which is why the defect survived; the relative leg is asserted in each self-test for exactly that reason, so a translator that breaks the common case fails too. Mutation proof: dropping the `$(sqlite3_dot_arg ...)` call leaves the relative leg green and takes the absolute leg to 0 backups (backup) and 2 rows instead of 1 (restore). A gate that cannot fail is decoration, and the sibling precedent is the same (`pg-receipt-selftest`, `scoped-ambient-reads-self-test`).

gates.label: Scoped authorization (H-1b)
gates._note: Added 2026-09-25 with the crate-audit round that found four authorization defects (BRIDGE-3, BRIDGE-5, BRIDGE-7 among them). verify-scoped-coverage.sh checks that a command HAS a _scoped twin and stops there: the moment a twin exists the command is 'covered' and the twin's BODY is never opened. So a _scoped fn that resolves a session and then reads or writes with no authorization at all passed that gate -- which is exactly how those defects survived. This gate checks the property: a _scoped fn reaching the store or the HAL must call a permission helper, be named in a reasoned list, or carry an `// ungated-ok:` marker in its body. Measured at introduction: 348 _scoped fns scanned, 0 unreasoned. The 35 explained entries split into deliberate shell asymmetry (promotions reads), documented module policy (tables, offline, scale, workspaces-picker), device-per-install values (license, health), and one KNOWN OPEN GAP deliberately NOT laundered as safe: the 9 hardware device commands (BRIDGE-7), where device access is currently open to any authenticated operator. Gating those is a product ruling, not a repair, so they carry a marker that says so. Runs in dev-ci.yml#static-gates, pre-push Tier 0 and scripts/check.sh.

gates.label: IPC parity
gates._note: Added 0.0.37. scripts/verify-ipc-parity.py enforces three directions. Forward: the UI invokes a command string absent from a shell's generate_handler![]. Reverse (backlog item 46): a shell registers a *_scoped command that no client invokes, so its permission check guards nothing -- the mirror of the gap the item-46 sweep kept finding, and the reason three SECURITY_MANAGE / SETTINGS_EDIT gates were mistaken for live security posture for several rounds. Both directions use dated allowlist sections (desktop/tablet, plus scoped_orphans for the reverse) and both self-clean, so neither list can accrete. Third direction, added 2026-09-18: an entry no direction reproduces -- production UI code names it nowhere and the shell does not register it -- now FAILS the run instead of being printed as info[<shell>-unreachable] while the run returned 0. It was the last population this file accepted and graded nothing about, and the three entries it found were deleted in the same change (desktop list_categories, list_products; tablet list_products -- the tablet's unscoped products command still exists in products.rs and stays an F-006 deletion candidate), so a shell section now carries measured gaps only and the entry counts went 11 -> 9 and 139 -> 138. Measured 2026-09-18: 441 UI command strings; desktop 455 registered / 9 unregistered UI names / 3 unregistered fns; tablet 320 registered / 138 unregistered UI names / 3 unregistered fns. The 25 allowlisted scoped orphans are a WORK QUEUE, not a clean bill -- most look like dead surface for F-006 to remove. --write-allowlist preserves sections it does not own. Runs in CI at dev-ci.yml#ipc-parity and in check.sh; the note claiming it local-only was itself stale and was corrected here. MOVED 2026-09-24: this gate and its --self-test left dev-ci.yml#static-gates for a job of their own, because the self-test measured 209s and 216s on two runs -- 33% of a job that also gated ~25 cheap checks. The real gate runs first in the new job so an actual parity violation still reports in ~30s; the self-test, which answers a rarer question, takes the slower slot. Path-gated on rust OR ui, since a parity break can only come from crates/, apps/*/src or ui/.

gates.label: PG receipt checker self-test
gates._note: Added 2026-09-27 with P0-2. verify-pg-tests-ran.py is the only reader of nextest's <flakyFailure> -- the shape in which a retry-rescued failure is recorded while the report's own totals still say failures="0", which is why a rerun-until-green suite can look clean. Its VERDICT has run per JUnit file in cargo-nextest since that step landed; its SELF-TEST ran in neither dev-ci.yml nor check.sh, so a regression inside the checker would have stayed invisible while every grade it produced still looked authoritative. That is not hypothetical: adding this step found the self-test RED -- the tree had grown to 88 skip arms across 16 files in 3 crates while ARM_BASELINE still read 84, so the census guard's own expectation had been firing on stale numbers (growth came from the kasirmu-api pg.rs split, whose pg_tests.rs alone holds 15). ARM_BASELINE moved 84 -> 88 in the same commit, per the contract at its own comment; ARM_FLOOR stayed at 65 deliberately, because raising a floor to track a bigger census erodes the headroom that absorbs a legitimate arm conversion. Same principle as auditor-selftests: a checker that cannot run is indistinguishable from a checker that found nothing.

gates.label: A11y regression (advisory)
gates._note: C24 correction. The old note said a11y was checked nowhere but locally, on the strength of `git grep a11y .github/workflows/dev-ci.yml` returning nothing. That grep was looking for a dedicated job and missed the real execution path: dev-ci.yml#ui-test (line ~467) runs `cd ui && npm test`, which is bare `vitest run`, and ui/vite.config.ts:129 excludes only ['e2e/**','node_modules/**'] -- so every file under src/__tests__/a11y/ runs in CI and an axe violation fails the job. Verified non-vacuously by injecting an unnamed <button> into a rendered subtree and watching the suite exit 1. This ENTRY is still advisory in the sense that check.sh's separate verbose re-run does not fail the gate; enforcement in CI is real and comes from ui-test, not from here. The genuine C24 gap is coverage: each screen's suite asserts a single rendered state, so conditional subtrees are never scanned (StaffLoginScreen is checked only on the username step, leaving the whole PIN pad unscanned).

gates._note: History worth keeping: this was declared 'required' while pointing at ci.yml#ci-docs-drift, a workflow retired to .bak by 23c96330, so it enforced nothing anywhere and the status was false. It was downgraded to 'advisory' when first wired into dev-ci.yml because the checker was reporting 68 items it had no vocabulary for. Two steps in each runner since 0.0.37: the drift check, and `--self-test`, which mutates four of the classifiers this gate depends on and requires each to be noticed, plus a control that must still pass. It exists because this is the gate that polices every other gate's CI claim and was the only one of the family without one, so "drift: 0 items" was indistinguishable from "the checker stopped looking" -- the failure that let the manifest rot. `ci.steps` is a list because the job has two relevant steps; singular `step` is only read by the advisory_at == "step" path.

gates.note: The fuzz job deliberately sets RUSTC_WRAPPER: '' in its job env. The ubuntu runner image globally wraps rustc with sccache, which breaks cargo-fuzz's --target build (its rustc version probe execs the resolved nightly toolchain path directly and dies with 'could not execute process sccache .../bin/rustc -vV'). The fuzz job is the only job affected (nightly + --target), so sccache must stay disabled there — do NOT re-add it. Caching is instead handled by Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with `workspaces: tools/fuzz` (cargo-fuzz builds into tools/fuzz/target/, which default workspace discovery misses).

gates.label: Fuzz targets typecheck
gates._note: Added 2026-09-27 with P0-3. This is deliberately NOT a restoration of the retired `fuzz` gate above, and the distinction is the point: the fuzzers do not RUN here. Seven targets sat in tools/fuzz compiled by nothing, and the rot was invisible because nothing could get far enough to report it — all four path dependencies read `../foundation`, `../crates/kasirmu-lua`, `../crates/kasirmu-core`, `../crates/kasirmu-plugin`, which resolve against tools/fuzz/Cargo.toml to tools/foundation et al. and do not exist. `cargo fuzz build` died at MANIFEST LOAD, before rustc ran, so there was no compile error to notice and no job to run one; the targets had been unreachable since the directory acquired its extra level. Fixed to `../../` and verified: `cargo check --bins --all-features` in tools/fuzz now finishes with zero errors across all seven (measured 2026-09-27), and `--all-features` is load-bearing because cart_deser, kasirpkg_parse and manifest_parse live behind kasirmu-core-fuzz / kasirmu-plugin-fuzz — a default-feature check would silently typecheck four of seven. A fuzz RUN stays out of reach for a different reason, recorded rather than papered over: libFuzzer + AddressSanitizer has no MSVC runtime in the nightly toolchain (`*asan*` under the Windows rustlib is empty), which makes the linked build Linux-only. Same shape as the `panic-inventory` entry: a target nothing compiles is indistinguishable from a target that compiles fine.

gates.label: Unsafe constructs carry a SAFETY comment
gates._note: Added 2026-09-28 with P3-3. P2-6 raised `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` from 7 to 38 of 43 crate roots, so the crates holding NO unsafe cannot grow any — but five legitimately keep it (kasirmu-logging syslog/eventlog FFI, kasirmu-security CredWriteW/CredReadW, kasirmu-hal JNI + Bluetooth, kasirmu-lua's Send/Sync impls, and the Tauri shells' `#[unsafe(link_section)]`), and a deny cannot protect those. Nothing else did either: measured 2026-09-27, no script and no gates.json entry mentioned SAFETY at all, so the only thing standing between a new unsafe block in those five and an unreviewed justification was the reviewer's eye. Now it is mechanical — `scripts/verify-unsafe-safety.py` fails any real construct without a `SAFETY:` comment, with a 18-case `--self-test`. LOCAL-ONLY for now: no CI step was added, so like `root policy` and `no-raw-params` this runs in `check.sh` and pre-push rather than on a PR. Adding a `static-gates` step is the natural follow-up and needs no code change, only a dev-ci.yml step. TWO MEASURED TRAPS the checker had to be taught, both recorded in its docstring: (a) grepping `unsafe` is nearly useless in this repo because the audit stamps are doc comments that say things like 'zero unsafe, no FFI/IO' and '8 unsafe blocks (not 6 — prior stamp miscount)' — an unanchored `unsafe impl` match flagged five sites in kasirmu-lua that were all PROSE about unsafe, two of them explaining that the crate deliberately does NOT implement it, and one a test assertion whose string literal starts with the phrase; (b) a strict same-or-adjacent-line rule for SAFETY produced 12 false positives because this repo documents a whole statement GROUP above the first of several calls (db_tests.rs:160-170 justifies four separate env calls in one block, windows.rs:66-73 justifies a block from six lines up). Hence the anchored arm, the comment-line filter, and the 12-line lookback.

gates.label: Rustdoc (deny warnings)
gates._note: Added 2026-09-28 with P2-4. Until this row, `cargo doc` had NO runner anywhere — not in check.sh, not in any live workflow, not in release.sh — so a broken intra-doc link was never a failure in any context. It is the exact shape of `rust-clippy` before C25 and `fuzz` before P0-3: a surface that looked covered because nothing reported on it. Measured 2026-09-28, the undeclared check was hiding 295 errors across 20 crates. SIX of them were not link noise but docs confidently describing something that does not exist: `KdsSyncEvent::OrderRecalled` (the variant is `Recalled`), `DriverRegistry::apply_config` (it is a FREE FUNCTION, not a method), `BridgeError::NotFound` (x3 — no such variant; the enum has Core/Hardware/Invalid/PermissionDenied/InvalidSession/TopologyValidation/Internal), `WebhookEndpoint::redacted` (no such method), and `get_setup_status` (x2 — the same file marks it REMOVED in a comment 10 lines above the link). THE ENV VAR AND THE RUNNER LANDED IN ONE COMMIT, and that is the whole point: `RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings` set on its own would have been a dead setting — rustdoc is the only reader, and with no `cargo doc` invocation it would have changed nothing while reading like a gate in review. Both halves or neither. TWO TRAPS this gate had to avoid, both measured rather than assumed: (1) the LOCAL step must pass `RUSTDOCFLAGS` inline — without it `cargo doc` reports warnings and STILL EXITS 0, so the step would be decoration that can never fail; (2) `--no-deps` is required, because without it a dependency's own doc warnings would fail this gate for a crate this repo does not own. CI runs `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` with the variable supplied by the workflow-level env block (dev-ci.yml:10-16); local runs supply it inline per step. The acceptance command `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` was verified to exit 0 with zero errors AND zero warnings before either half landed — the ordered acceptance in P2-4 is what kept this from being a red gate on every PR, and it is worth keeping in mind for the next gate added this way.

gates.label: kasirmu-core size ratchet
gates._note: Added 2026-10-05 (round 148). This step has been in check.sh with a full rationale at line 524-533 and NO gates.json record, which is the structural blind spot the bundle-parity note describes: verify-ci-docs-drift.py iterates the gates present in the manifest, so a gate with no row can never be reported as required-but-not-enforced. Found by running every checker and asking why one FAILED rather than assuming; the failure itself was another session in-flight core work, but the missing row was real. The ratchet counts non-blank production lines under crates/kasirmu-core/src, minus whole test files and inline #[cfg(test)] mod blocks, and fails when the count rises above scripts/core-size-baseline.json. Mutation-proven: adding three lines to audit.rs fails with +3. LOWERING the ceiling is a deliberate edit in a commit that says why, the same shape as namespace-governance-baseline.json. NOTE it is environment-INDEPENDENT but tree-DEPENDENT: it fails whenever any session has in-flight core growth, so a red run in a shared checkout is not automatically yours -- check `git status --porcelain -- crates/kasirmu-core` first.

gates.label: Per-crate coverage floors
gates._note: Added 2026-09-27 with P1-2. Coverage INSTRUMENTATION has existed for a long time (scripts/coverage.sh, cargo-llvm-cov, HTML + lcov output) and coverage ENFORCEMENT did not: the script prints a percentage and exits 0 whatever the number is, and the `coverage` gate above has been `retired` since ci.yml was renamed to .bak. A report nobody reads cannot fire. This closes that, on the rule the checklist states for itself -- 'an unrecorded threshold is not a threshold' -- so the figure lives in scripts/coverage-floors.json rather than in prose. PER-CRATE, not a workspace average, because P1-2 says a global average 'hides the crates that matter' and the measurement bears it out: measured 2026-09-27, foundation 99.4%, kasirmu-core 83.8%, modules-inventory 78.4%, platform-sync 68.7%, workspace 73.9%. A single 70% floor would have passed with platform-sync -- the crate this checklist calls the highest-risk surface -- dropping a full point, because foundation's 99.4% carried it. Each floor sits 2 points BELOW its measured value: a ratchet that freezes the level reached and fires on regression, not a target that goes red on day one and teaches people to ignore it. The checker is unit-tested in both directions (`--self-test`, 13 cases, including that a 95% workspace average still fails a 60% crate and that summing cannot become averaging). Two constraints worth naming: cargo llvm-cov RUNS THE SUITE and aborts on any failing test (measured: an unrelated in-flight failure in kasirmu-bridge aborted a workspace run), so in check.sh a measurement failure is reported as 'could not measure' rather than 'coverage regressed' -- those are different problems; and the job needs the same system dependencies as cargo-nextest because it links the workspace.

gates._note: Added 0.0.37: the gate existed in both runners and had no record here, which is the exact blind spot this manifest exists to close -- its own description says adding a gate here is the ONLY way to add a gate, yet check.sh:245 (`step "release version gate"`) and dev-ci.yml#release-readiness were both already invoking `node scripts/check-release-version.mjs --self-test`. gates.label: Updater signature verifier
gates._note: Added 0.0.37. scripts/verify-updater-signature.mjs (AUDIT-28 RELEASE-04/06) is the post-build check the release workflow runs BEFORE PUBLISHING: it verifies an installer against the signature in latest.json using the pubkey committed in tauri.conf.json, so a release can never go live with a signature that does not verify. Security-critical and previously the only uncatalogued gate of the four -- its neighbours release-version and updater-manifest were both reachable (the latter via release-readiness, which names the script). Its own tool is named by no gate and its label matched no needle. Local-only for the self-test: the real verification runs inside release.yml. Ships with --self-test including tamper rejection.

gates.label: Release workflow validation
gates._note: R36-11. release.yml was renamed to release.yml.bak by 23c96330 with an empty commit message and nothing replaced it, so pushing a v* tag produced no installers for a whole release cycle. A workflow that never runs cannot report its own breakage, so this validates statically what needs no tag, key material, or macOS/Windows runner: action pins, referenced paths, docker residue left by the desktop-only restore, an inventory gate demanding an artifact no matrix entry builds, and that a missing UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY still hard-fails rather than publishing an unsigned manifest every client rejects. Ships with --self-test (8 mutations) so a regression cannot silently turn it into a no-op.

gates.label: Release readiness
gates._note: Runs scripts/check-updater-compat.mjs, which builds a Rust harness pinned to the minisign-verify version the real Tauri updater client uses and proves that signatures from generate-latest-json.mjs VERIFY, that a tampered installer is REJECTED, and that the pubkey committed in tauri.conf.json parses. Before this it ran ONLY inside release.yml.bak, i.e. nowhere at all -- so the signing chain could have rotted silently alongside the retired workflow and the first symptom would be customers unable to auto-update. Path-gated on the release toolchain and the updater pubkey because the harness needs a cold cargo build. No `runners` key: that field names LOCAL entry points, and this one needs a cargo build, so it is CI-only. DEPLOY COUPLING IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT (2026-09-14): `northflank-deploy` deliberately omits this gate from its `needs` -- that deploy POSTs the commit sha to Northflank, which builds ops/docker/Dockerfile.unified, a BACKEND container consuming no installer, no latest.json and no updater pubkey, while release.yml gates this chain where it binds (release-validate runs the same scripts/check-updater-compat.mjs, release-build needs release-validate, release-publish needs release-build). Adding the edge here would bind 100% of deploys to a check unrelated to the artifact shipped, because the changes router forces release=true on every non-PR event while the release router paths held 140 of 7,841 commits over the last 90 days (1.79%), and because its own failure surface (an unstable rust-toolchain pin, node 24, a cold cargo build under the workflow-wide RUSTFLAGS) can stop a deploy it cannot affect; narrowing the route instead is a no-op on the deploy path. Read `status` as POLICY, not as a deploy graph: required-by-policy and not-a-deploy-prerequisite are both true at once, so the missing `needs` edge is this note, not a bug to file. Residual risk, stated: `main` is unprotected, so a red run of this gate is still mergeable.

gates.label: EOL guard
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36 (R36-15). The pre-commit line-ending step filtered on 'git check-attr text' alone, which is wrong twice: it ignored '.gitattributes *.bat text eol=crlf' and stripped CRLF from the working tree (producing a phantom-dirty git status with zero content diff), and because '* text=auto' reports 'auto' for every path including binaries, a staged PNG had the 0D 0A in its signature deleted and the mangled blob re-staged -- verified on apps/desktop-tauri/icons/32x32.png, 1515 to 1507 bytes. Both are silent corruption behind a green hook. The test extracts the live guard from .githooks/pre-commit rather than copying it, so it cannot drift from what it polices, and it fails loudly if either guard disappears.

gates.label: typecheck gate
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. Guards the UI typecheck step of .githooks/pre-commit, which was added after ten commits landed with HEAD failing tsc -- Vitest injects describe/it/expect/beforeEach/vi at runtime, so a missing import passes 'npm run test' and only fails 'tsc --noEmit', and nothing ran that before commit. The step fires only when a commit stages ui/src TypeScript, so on a Rust-only or docs-only stretch it goes unexercised and is indistinguishable from a step someone deleted; this test extracts the live step from the hook and drives it against a throwaway repo with a stubbed npm, asserting it triggers on nested .ts/.tsx, stays off for CSS/Rust/CI/docs-only and empty indexes, honours KASIRMU_SKIP_TYPECHECK=1, aborts with rc=1 on a failing typecheck, and warns rather than silently passing when ui/node_modules is absent.

gates.label: typecheck tripwire
gates._note: Promoted 2026-09-30. scripts/test-typecheck-tripwire.sh policed the SECOND typecheck guard in .githooks/post-commit -- the one that fires after a commit stages ui/src TypeScript -- and was wired to NO runner at all, in check.sh or in any workflow. The sibling test for the pre-commit step of the same name (test-typecheck-gate.sh) has been a required gate since 0.0.37, so the two guards looked equally defended and one was not. The tripwire defends the failure modes the pre-commit gate cannot see: a pathspec matching nothing, a block placed BELOW one of the hook's four early `exit 0` paths, and a verdict written when npm never ran. It extracts the live block between the '# tripwire-start' and '# tripwire-end' markers rather than reimplementing the trigger, so a copy in the test would pass forever while the real tripwire silently never ran. Measured cost under a second with only npm stubbed and a throwaway git repo, so it belongs beside its siblings in the job that already runs nine of them.

gates.label: records index escaping
gates._note: Promoted 2026-09-30. scripts/test-records-index-escaping.sh policed the cell sanitizer in scripts/generate-records-index.mjs -- the guard that stops a record label containing '](x)' from becoming a fabricated link in docs/records/README.md -- and was wired to NO runner. The generator itself does run, in ci-docs-drift, but that step is `--check`, which is happy with whatever the generator writes, so it can only ever say the output is faithful to the input; it says nothing about whether a hostile label is neutralised. An escaping regression would have shipped a generator that still regenerated its own index perfectly. The test drives the LIVE generator through KASIRMU_RECORDS_ROOT and then a frozen deliberately-unfixed one that MUST fail the same exploit assertion, which is what makes a green run evidence rather than a tautology. Measured 2.3s, and it writes only inside a mktemp dir.

gates.label: post-commit index guard
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. Guards .githooks/post-commit, which refreshes the codebase-memory graph every commit and had been dead for 535 commits (2026-09-05 01:32 to 2026-09-08) with nothing anywhere reporting it. Two causes, both invisible at commit time: it resolved the indexer off PATH, landing on the stale %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs build that refuses to join a newer running daemon (30s handshake timeout), and it sent that failure to /dev/null. A third, unrelated hazard was found while proving the fix: a file literally named 'nul' in the repo root -- what '2> nul' creates under Git bash, unlike cmd.exe -- aborts the indexer's discovery pass in ~2s before .cbmignore is consulted, so the whole root index fails with a generic 'Pipeline failed'. The test extracts the live resolve and ghost-quarantine blocks from the hook via markers rather than copying them, so it cannot drift from what it polices, and it FATALs if a marker disappears instead of passing vacuously. It asserts versioned-over-PATH precedence, numeric (not lexical) version ordering, both pin env vars, that PATH and the legacy install remain reachable as fallbacks, that untracked reserved-name ghosts are relocated to .git/cbm-ghosts while tracked paths are never touched, that no index output is pointed at /dev/null, that the hook is mode 100755 in the index, and end to end that a real 'git hook run post-commit' writes a start line, captures the indexer's stdout, records a zero exit status, clears a ghost, and honours CBM_SKIP_POST_COMMIT=1.

gates.label: AGENTS.md mirror truthfulness
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36. Two copies of the agent rules exist (root AGENTS.md, .agents/AGENTS.md); a third, .prime/AGENTS.md, was deleted with the .prime/ tree on 08-09-26 and its per-mirror mutation table went with it. scripts/bump-version.ps1 syncs only their version lines -- the file itself documents that nothing syncs the gate list. Twice in this release a mirror stated something the repo contradicted: .agents/AGENTS.md kept saying 'Steps 6, 7 and 8 have no CI backstop' after 13f2a1dc put Go into dev-ci.yml#static-gates, and root AGENTS.md claimed dev-ci 'runs on every PR and push' when it has no push trigger at all. The first is the mirror that governs work under .agents/, so an agent following it would believe Go changes are unguarded. Required and CI-blocking from day one, unlike ci-docs-drift, because it has no baseline and no pre-existing failures: ground truth is read from .githooks/pre-commit, .github/workflows/*.yml and Cargo.toml rather than asserted, so adding a gate or bumping the version updates the expectation without touching the checker. --self-test mutates each mirror and requires a named finding; a mutation that changes nothing is reported WRONG rather than passing silently, which is how the .prime phrasing gap was found and closed. RETIREMENT 2026-09-29: the second copy, .agents/management/AGENTS.md, was deleted 2026-09-24 by 5ec0ca164 -- a commit whose whole change was that deletion -- so MIRRORS now holds root AGENTS.md alone, bump-version.ps1 no longer writes a second version-lock line, and a retired path in that list is reported as a missing one rather than read as agreement. (The deletion was recorded, not reverted: manager-codebase-review-checklist.md:723 already finds no live target to repoint to.)

gates.label: Conventional-commit subjects
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36. .githooks/commit-msg has enforced the subject format locally since 9cf14190, but core.hooksPath is set by setup-dev.ps1 and is not versioned, so a clone that skips setup gets no subject gate -- a limitation the hook's own header states and defers to a future CI check. This closes that. The rule is extracted from the hook at run time (TYPES, PATTERN, and the Merge/Revert/fixup/squash/amend exemptions) rather than duplicated, so local and CI cannot drift into disagreeing about what is legal; each extractor raises rather than returning an empty set, because an empty exemption list would reject every merge commit and an empty type list would accept anything. Commits older than the hook's own introduction are skipped, derived via `git log --diff-filter=A -- .githooks/commit-msg` rather than a hardcoded sha, and the skipped count is printed so the grandfathering is visible. Verified against the four commits the hook header names as its motivation (2eea3d07, faa5dae0, 5855c429, 84a71f3e): all four are found, all four are pre-rule, and the 77 commits since the hook conform. The CI step needs fetch-depth 0 -- with the default depth of 1 the range is empty and the gate would pass by checking nothing.

gates.label: PG schema drift guard
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. 20260813_init.pg.sql is GENERATED by this script from the SQLite migrations and must never be hand-edited. The job lived in ci.yml, which 23c96330 renamed to .bak with no replacement, and it was restored neither in dev-ci.yml nor in check.sh -- so the only guard was pre-commit step 7, and core.hooksPath is set by scripts/setup-dev.ps1 and is not versioned. On a clone that skips setup, a stale or hand-edited generated file committed and merged clean. `--check` is a pure text comparison: no Docker, no psycopg, no sqlite handle, ~1s. Note the asymmetry this closes is not that the gate was weak, but that it had NO gates.json record at all, so verify-ci-docs-drift.py could not report a gate that is required but not enforced -- it never learned the gate existed.

gates.label: Migration column types

Run here WITHOUT --staged-only, which is what the hook uses -- CI must scan all 28 migration files, not whatever one commit happened to touch, or a float column shipped by a hook-less clone is never revisited. ~0.1s.

gates.label: i18n bundle parity
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. This is pre-commit step 4 and had NO gates.json record until then, which is a worse failure than pointing at a retired workflow: verify-ci-docs-drift.py iterates the gates present in the manifest, so a gate with no record can never be reported as required-but-not-enforced. The blind spot is structural, not a data error. It is also the step whose own history is the worst -- before the Fluent page audit it walked only literal <Localized id> under ui/src/features/** and skipped every shared-chrome and context file it was handed, so 14 broken keys shipped while it reported clean. --scan-dirs is load-bearing: the tool defaults to `features` alone, and the directories named add 108 files (428 -> 536, 25% more coverage; re-measured 2026-09-18 -- the +108 delta has held, the absolutes had rotted from 228/336 and the old 47% with them). A runner that omits the flag prints '0 missing key(s)' over a fifth of the surface unexamined. The list lives in THREE executable copies -- this note, dev-ci.yml's step, scripts/check.sh, and scripts/verify-bundle-parity.py's CENSUS_SCAN_DIRS (reached by the pre-push hook via --full-census) -- and the restructure campaign's P2 deleted two of the named directories (`frontend`, `platform`) on 2026-09-17 without updating any of them, which made the gate exit 2 'scan dir not found' on every push and in CI until 2026-09-18. CI and check.sh deliberately run WITHOUT --staged-only, which the hook uses: a key reference shipped by a hook-less clone must be revisited by something.

gates.label: ftl attribute requests
gates._note: Added 2026-10-05. Closes the class verify-bundle-parity.py declares OUT OF SCOPE at its own docstring: that checker validates message IDs, not the ATTRIBUTES a call site asks for via attrs={{...}}. When a message defines no .placeholder, @fluent/react falls back to the between-tag children -- a hardcoded English literal -- so the component renders, the suite passes, and the translation that exists in *.id.ftl is never shown. Three messages shipped that way and were fixed in d9cc0098f. All three real findings sat behind a DYNAMIC id (id={flag ? a : b}), which is why the checker resolves BOTH branches; a resolver keyed on the nearest LITERAL id produced three false positives first, which is the trap worth knowing about. Unresolvable sites (id={JS_VAR}) are counted and printed rather than skipped, so the coverage cannot look wider than it is.

gates.label: Runner label integrity
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. verify-ci-docs-drift.py checked each gate's `runners` labels with has_needle(), which is ANY-of: a gate declaring three labels was satisfied by one. Deleting the other two from check.sh left the manifest asserting guards that no longer existed while the checker printed '0 drift item(s)'. Demonstrated against this repo's own ci-docs-drift gate, which declares both 'ci docs drift' and 'ci docs drift self-test' -- removing the self-test step changed nothing. The rule is now missing_needles(), which reports every label matching nothing; adopting it was safe precisely because the manifest was accurate under the stricter reading (all 5 multi-label gates resolved every label), so this closed a latent gap rather than converting it into false failures. Two properties the test encodes because both produced confident wrong answers first: ROOT derives from __file__ not cwd, so a fixture that omits the checker itself reads the real repo and agrees with itself; and needles match by substring, so a short label cannot fail while a longer one containing it exists.

gates.label: Exhaustive-deps ratchet
gates._note: Caps react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings at the value in scripts/exhaustive-deps-baseline.json (7, down from 12). `npm run lint` is `eslint .` with no --max-warnings 0, so it exits 0 while reporting 58 warnings, and this rule is the only automated check for a stale closure. Item 69 found five callbacks listing `userId` -- a prop no component body ever read, kept 'used' only by its presence in the deps array -- while two of those same arrays omitted `promotionIds`, which IS sent in the complete_sale payload. Neither was gated by anything. The ratchet does not clear the debt, it freezes the improvement. Runs in ui-test rather than static-gates because it needs ui/node_modules, which only ui-test and i18n install. Like the FTL orphan gate its CI value depends on the job actually running, and dev-ci.yml has no push trigger, so on a long-lived release branch check.sh remains the only thing enforcing it.

gates.label: Server origin consistency
gates._note: Added in 0.0.39. Reads the compiled origin list in crates/kasirmu-core/src/server_origin.rs (ADR #55) and fails when a Tauri CSP, the Worker CSP, the Worker LICENSE_API_URL fallback, the settings draft, or either Rust dev fallback disagrees with it. The drift it guards was live: the compiled auth URL said license.kasir.mu while both Tauri CSPs, the desktop bootstrap, the settings draft and the runbook all said license.ozpos.my.id, so a host change silently needed a release and nothing detected the mismatch. gates.label: shell syntax
gates._note: Added 2026-09-29. A shell file that does not parse does not RUN, so every step inside it is skipped and nothing reports that; the pre-commit hook case is sharper, because a hook that cannot parse stops gating everything it was written to gate. sh -n parses without executing, so this is safe to run first, on a bare checkout, and cannot have side effects. Paid for itself on its first run: scripts/profile.sh line 151 read "fi# -- Build and run command", and since bash treats # as a comment only when it STARTS a word, "fi#" lexes as one token, the enclosing if never closed, and bash reported it at END OF FILE 65 lines away with every keyword, quote, brace and $( in the file balancing. Covers all first-party .sh repo-wide and excludes vendored trees.

gates.label: powershell syntax
gates._note: Added 2026-09-30, the shell gate's twin for the language shell's scope rule cannot reach. That rule is a shebang, read as a fact about the file, and PowerShell has no shebang -- so 26 tracked .ps1 files were parsed by nothing, including ops/install/win/{install,uninstall}.ps1 which run on a USER's machine. A separate file rather than a flag: putting a parser-per-language switch inside is_shell() would mean every future Windows question had to be answered in a file named for shells. Paid for itself on the class it was written for: scripts/profile.ps1 had a backtick inside a double-quoted string, and backtick is PowerShell's ESCAPE, so the closing quote was itself escaped, the string never terminated, and the parser reported it 65 lines later as 'The string is missing the terminator' plus a phantom 'Missing closing }'. ParseFile is an AST parse and never executes, so it is as safe to run first as sh -n. Refuses with exit 2 when neither pwsh nor powershell is present, and when it finds no .ps1 at all: a clean run must be distinguishable from a starved one.

gates.label: workflow syntax
gates._note: Added 2026-09-29, the shell gate's sibling. A .github/workflows/*.yml that is not valid YAML runs NO JOBS AT ALL: GitHub reports the workflow errored and executes none of them, so the failure presents as a green PR that stopped checking rather than a red one. Only release.yml had a syntax check before this (verify-release-workflow.py); dev-ci.yml, android.yml and website.yml had none. Also rejects three shapes that are valid YAML but invalid as workflows -- non-mapping top level, no jobs key, and jobs that is empty or a list -- because "it parsed" is the most misleading possible green. Refuses to report clean when it finds no workflows (exit 2). The attic is excluded deliberately: a retired .bak is never executed.

gates.label: self-tests wired
gates._note: Added 2026-09-29. Answers one question: does a checker's --self-test have a caller? A self-test no runner invokes rots in silence -- the cases still pass by hand and nothing says nobody runs them. Measured when it was written: 24 of 28 scripts/verify-*.py declared a --self-test and NINE were invoked from no runner at all; one of the nine had been printing "nothing calls this flag" in its own report. Deliberately narrow: it does not decide WHICH runner should invoke one, or whether a given self-test is any good, and a check.sh-only caller counts. It also ships with the bug class it was written to catch, found in the gate three times before it was right: a COMMENT mentioning the flag counted as a caller; a RETIRED .bak workflow counted as a caller; and the scope covered only verify-*.py, so check-*.py was invisible. Full-line comments are stripped, attic/ is excluded, and the scope is now verify-*/check-*.

gates.label: settled-read copies
gates._note: Added 2026-09-30. The settled-read contract -- a failed read returns { ok: false } with no value, so a caller cannot mistake it for "answered, and the answer was empty" -- reached FOUR hand-copied implementations before any check could see them: BootRead in app/AppShell.tsx, BootReadResult in utils/boot-retry.ts, Read in stock-transfers/StockTransfersScreen.tsx and warehouse/WarehouseCountFlow.tsx. Each was type-correct, each passed the whole suite, and two documented the contract by citing a COPY at a line range that had already moved. Nothing in scripts/ referenced settleRead at all, so the fifth copy would have arrived the same silent way. Shape-based, not name-based: naming those four in a list would make the checker report zero findings the day after it was written, which is how the first four got there. It grades declarations only -- a caller may legitimately name the type in a signature -- and it does not judge whether a second verdict SHAPE is ever warranted; boot-retry.ts keeps its own function because a read that must be RE-ISSUED against a timeout cannot reuse settleRead, and this checker is what records that the distinction is deliberate rather than accidental.

gates.label: checker self-test companions
gates._note: Added 2026-09-29. Each step here is the LIVENESS PROOF for a gate named in the same row: the cases that prove the gate can still FAIL, which no bare run of the gate can see. The convention, stated at 'IPC command parity self-test' in dev-ci.yml, is that a checker's self-test lives beside the checker it proves. This row exists because gates.json had no reverse-direction check -- test-runner-labels.py grades gates.json -> check.sh and never asks whether a step that EXISTS has a row -- so wiring them was silent, and an inventory that understates the matrix is the same quiet-drift problem as a gate that cannot see half its input. These were each mutation-proven: a regex or pattern pointed at something that cannot match, which must turn the case red rather than reporting zero. Two of the seventeen (doc uniqueness self-test, release workflow self-test) pre-date this row and were ALREADY unlisted when it was written -- the drift was not introduced by the 2026-09 work, only measured by it.

gates.label: local matrix checkers
gates._note: Added 2026-09-29 to close the 7 gate steps that ran in check.sh with no row. These are checkers, not setup: npm ci, website npm ci, test workspace (nextest), test application shells and their siblings are deliberately NOT listed here, and that is the reason no blanket reverse check exists. check.sh mixes gates with INSTALLS and TEST-RUNNER invocations, and deciding which is which is a judgement per step, not a rule -- so a naive 'every step needs a row' check would fire on 13 correct entries and get muted on its first run. Which is the shape of the mistake this campaign has made repeatedly: a check broad enough to be easy is narrow enough to be useless. Each step listed here runs a scripts/*.py checker with a --self-test beside it, and verify-selftests-wired.py is what keeps that pairing true from now on.

A `TODO 2a` in a comment is invisible to the compiler, to the test suite, and to check-dead-refs.py (which grades packages and paths, not debt ids), so the repo accumulated two distinct failures with no gate to catch either: a marker whose work already shipped is a dead pointer, and a marker whose id resolves to no plan is a citation to a document nobody can open. gates.label: Browser SDK types vs published OpenAPI
gates._note: Added 2026-09-30. ui/src/api/client/types.ts opens with a header saying every type in it is derived from the OpenAPI 3.1 specification. Nothing derived them and nothing graded them. A manual census on 2026-09-30 found 5 of the 15 interfaces present on both sides had drifted: CategoryDto carried created_at (the row has no timestamp, and the REQUIRED icon was missing instead), TokenResponse was missing token_id, SyncStatusResponse invented conflict_count and total_items (neither exists on the wire), CreateTokenRequest could not express the ADR sync-auth-hardening client-credentials path, ProductDetail lacked image_hash and images, and SaleStatus lacked pending. The worst was not a stale field but a wrong SHAPE: create_token_handler answers a token envelope and the client typed the envelope as the details, so every Authorization header built from it would have carried a stringified object. Repaired in the commit before this one, and this checker then found a SIXTH the census had missed -- HealthResponse was omitting rls_posture and portable_derivation_uses_master_key, both always sent -- because the census extractor mis-parsed the same file. Required rather than advisory so 0 findings is a baseline a flip can be measured from. Only names present on BOTH sides are compared: the document describes two servers while types.ts describes the one the browser talks to, so a two-way set comparison would be a permanent red page, and the one-sided names are reported as context instead. Exits 2 rather than 0 when an input cannot be parsed, so a checker that could not run never reads as one that found nothing.
gates._parser_note: The extractors read a Rust json! literal out of a .rs file, which is not JSON. Three inputs in these two files break a naive reader, and each was found by running the checker against the live tree rather than by reasoning about it: line comments between schema entries (one contains a JSON example, whose braces a scanner counts as structure, which is how PushOutcome lost its own name), a Rust expression embedded as a value (apps/cloud-server/src/openapi/cloud.rs carries env! with CARGO_PKG_VERSION as an example), and a description string containing escaped quotes. Comments are blanked before scanning rather than removed, so every offset and line number survives; a macro invocation is skipped as one token, the way a string is. The self-test covers the scanner cases and the classify cases and touches no files, so it cannot rot when the tree is renamed.

gates.label: Positional row-mapper alignment
gates._note: Added 2026-10-04. `name: row.get(3)?` couples a mapper to its SQL by POSITION and nothing in Rust checks that coupling: reorder the projection, insert a column, or copy a mapper onto a new struct and the fields silently take each other's values -- every one present, correctly typed, and wrong. Not hypothetical: run_list_credit_sales (crates/kasirmu-bridge/src/settings/core.rs) reads index 1, `p.gateway_reference`, into `customer_name`, the field the retail credit list renders in a Customer column (ui/src/features/retail/RetailModals.tsx), so an operator reads a payment reference where the buyer's name belongs. It survived because the pin covering that type builds the DTO from hand-written literals -- a wire-shape pin that never runs a query, so it cannot see the mapping. The checker pairs each mapper block with the statement feeding it and compares the Nth column against the field name. ONE mismatch is acknowledged and reported each run without failing it: choosing which column a customer name should come from is a product ruling, not a repair, and the record is docs/records/JOURNAL.md (2026-10-04, a3c871787). The suppression is keyed by (file, field), so any OTHER mapper with the same defect still fails -- verified by re-running the checker against a copy of that mapper under a different path, where it reports and exits 1. Required rather than advisory so 0 findings is a baseline a flip can be measured from. Exits 2 on a refused --roots list, so a starved corpus never reads as a clean tree.

gates.label: COR-7 replay fork control set
gates._note: Added 2026-10-05. The tablet command layer is a fork of the desktop one, so the per-attempt idempotency rules (COR-7) exist twice -- kasirmu-bridge/src/pos/checkout/replay.rs and apps/mobile-tauri/src/commands/pos/checkout.rs -- and the fork's own header says 'a second implementation of the SAME rules ... keep them in step'. Nothing checked that, and they drifted into a SECURITY defect: only the bridge refused a colon in the attempt id (validated_attempt_id), which is what stops a crafted `a:rekey:b` from composing a base key byte-identical to another attempt's re-key LOOKUP key and making the replay guard answer with a sale the basket never rang up (1596631d2). The trim half of the same contract stayed in step ONLY because `whitespace_only_attempt_id_is_unguarded_like_the_tablet` pinned it, so the failure mode is precisely a rule added to one fork without a cross-shell pin. The checker pins the CONTROL SET and not the bodies: the fork returns a different error type (AppError vs BridgeError) and legitimately diverges in behaviour, so a body diff would over-report, but a control present on one side only is always a regression. Exits 2 on a refused --root so a starved corpus never reads as a clean tree. NOT gating the tablet's missing re-key EPOCH counter: that is the Rekey-vs-refuse product ruling plus a missing port, not a control that can be required today.

gates.label: Gate roster runner claims
gates._note: Added 2026-10-05. scripts/gates.json records, per gate, which step in check.sh and which step in dev-ci.yml runs it, and NOTHING compared those claims, so they rot: the coverage-floors entry declared a CI step named 'Generate coverage report' that has never existed -- dev-ci.yml has carried 'Coverage report' since e44fed2b2 -- so an auditor reading the roster would conclude the gate has no CI runner when it does. This gate is the roster auditing itself. It matches decorated step names by PREFIX (check.sh spells some steps 'clippy workspace' and 'no-raw-params (ADR #7 Phase 4)'), does NOT treat a hyphen as a decorator (skill-drift-guard is a different step from skill-drift), downgrades a runner that runs INLINE rather than through step() to a note (five do: invoke-token-parity, no-hardcoded-money-format, skill-drift, a11y-advisory, audit) so a working gate is not reported broken, and honours a _runner_note (panic-inventory). Ships with --self-test, 10 cases, because a checker that cannot fail is worse than none -- and writing it DID find a real flaw in the first draft matcher, recorded in the script.

gates.label: Module namespace governance (soft)
gates._note: Added 2026-09-30 (Round 4 of the modular-scaffolding plan, Immediate Next Action 3). ADR-62 named the module seams; docs/architecture/module-namespace-governance.md names the rules and this enforces the mechanical half of them SOFTLY. Rule 1 (no new cross-vertical raw SQL outside the reporting facade) fails only on a NEW edge -- the two edges that exist are frozen in scripts/namespace-governance-baseline.json: modules/reporting/src/repository.rs reads sales directly (known facade-bypass debt, plan 9.5) and modules/loyalty/src/repository.rs reads gift_cards while loyalty declares only [crm] (found by this inventory, not surfaced by the plan). Rule 2 (no new unclassified handler) fails a type absent from scripts/handler-classification.json, populated from the Phase 0 census (docs/records/superseded/handler-census-phase0.md) with the ADR-62 D4 vocabulary. Rule 3 (undeclared dependency) is informational, not blocking, because real edges exist today. Style is deliberately soft, not strict: every module shares one SQLite connection, so a namespace boundary is a convention rather than a mechanically expressible property, and strict enforcement is deferred to Phase 4. The checker reads table names OUT of Rust string literals (a mask-strings-first scanner finds nothing, which is how the first draft reported 0 of 2 known edges); it carries --self-test, and the pair is listed under checker-selftest-companions via verify-selftests-wired.py. | Updated 2026-10-03 (Phase 4 P4.5): the gate step now runs --strict (scripts/check.sh), so an undeclared dependency (Rule 3) blocks instead of being informational. Strictness is safe because the population was clean at flip time (0 undeclared edges; 1 frozen cross-vertical edge, baselined and grant-marked).

gates.label: Capability parity (manifest capabilities)
gates._note: Added 2026-10-03 (Phase 4 P4.1 of the modular-scaffolding plan). A module manifest's `capabilities` array was free text, so a grant for a namespace the module does not own and does not declare as a dependency read exactly like a legitimate one. This gate makes the set mechanical: `read:<id>` + `write:<id>` when the module owns tables in modules/ownership.json, plus `read:<dep>` for every entry in its `dependencies`. verify-namespace-governance.py --check-capabilities derives the expected set for all 14 manifests (36 capabilities) and fails on any drift; --emit-capabilities rewrites them. It is the manifest half of the strict enforcement Phase 4 targets -- the runtime NamespacedStore check in crates/kasirmu-core is the other half, and the two must agree on the same ownership map.

gates.label: Ownership map parity (single source)
gates._note: Added 2026-10-02 (Phase 2 of the modular-scaffolding plan, resolving the NamespacedStore draft section 7). The table->module ownership map had TWO hand-maintained copies (docs/architecture/module-namespace-governance.md section 3 prose and TABLE_OWNERS in scripts/verify-namespace-governance.py); Phase 2 needs a third copy in Rust so the runtime NamespacedStore check can consult the same map, and a third hand-maintained list is exactly what drifts. So the map now has ONE source, modules/ownership.json: scripts/generate-ownership-map.mjs generates crates/kasirmu-core/src/db/ownership.rs from it (--check fails on drift) and verify-namespace-governance.py --check-ownership fails when its TABLE_OWNERS disagrees. Three consumers, one source, pinned by a Rust unit test (crates/kasirmu-core/src/db/ownership_tests.rs) and a Python self-test (mutation fixtures for duplicate-table and empty-map). Local-only runner today; adding a dev-ci.yml step needs no code change.

gates.label: Core size ratchet
gates._note: Added 2026-10-03 (Phase 3 P3.4 of the modular-scaffolding plan, section 11.1). The plan's boundary rule for extraction has a number: crates/kasirmu-core must not grow as modules move out. Without a measured ceiling the extraction is reversible by accident -- new logic lands back in core and nothing notices, because a codebase that is 'smaller than yesterday' has no yesterday. scripts/verify-core-size.py counts NON-BLANK production lines under crates/kasirmu-core/src, excluding whole test files (*_tests.rs, tests.rs, any tests/ directory) and inline #[cfg(test)] mod blocks, with comments and string bodies masked first; scripts/core-size-baseline.json records the ceiling (36590 across 176 files). The checker FAILS when the count rises above the ceiling and reports the headroom when it falls, so LOWERING the ceiling is a deliberate edit in a commit that says why -- exactly how a retired namespace edge leaves scripts/namespace-governance-baseline.json. Mutation-proven: adding three production lines to crates/kasirmu-core/src/audit.rs fails with +3, removing them passes. The self-test is a separate step because verify-selftests-wired.py is what keeps that pairing true.

gates._note: Wired 2026-10-02, after repairing the detector rather than before. gates.label: CI claims in documentation
gates._note: Wired 2026-10-02, after the same repair-then-wire order. The checker grades CI job and step names asserted in prose against the live workflows. All seven of its findings were inside docs/records/superseded/ and docs/records/audits/ - dated records describing the retired ci-pipeline doc - so those folders joined SKIP_DIR, mirroring ARCHIVE_PREFIXES in verify-doc-uniqueness.py. Scan scope measured before and after: 473 docs to 410, the 63 dated records excluded, 410 still graded. Its 80-line lookahead was also a bug worth naming: northflank-deploy carries its steps: 98 lines below its key, so the job fell out of the live set and a CORRECT runbook was reported as claiming a job no workflow defines.
